review_evidence: README describes a backend- and SQL-independent relational database client with model/query/migration APIs.

Only 10 of 35 Lean files contain proposition/example declarations; inspection shows these are internal indexing/string/hash-map lemmas, schema-equivalence decidability, migration-recipe validity and compile-time/examples supporting the client implementation.

The migration structures and proofs do not specify or verify SQL/database execution semantics against an external model; the project’s substantive purpose is executable client/metaprogramming infrastructure.

source_action.content_invariant: All 35 Lean files were scanned and the proposition-bearing modules inspected. Theorems concern string/index equivalences, hash-map helpers, schema/migration recipe validity and executable examples; there is no formal SQL/backend semantics or end-to-end query/migration correctness theory separate from the software implementation.
evidence: README explicitly identifies a backend-independent relational database client library.

Migration/Basic.lean defines internal indexing/schema equivalence and migration data, with supporting decidability theorems; Recipe.lean packages hash-map operations and validity witnesses for executable migrations.
The remaining proposition-bearing files are utility/client implementation lemmas and examples, not an independent formalization corpus.
source_action.rationale: The repository is a general-purpose relational database client and metaprogrammed query/migration DSL; its propositions serve implementation invariants and decidability machinery rather than an independently addressable database-semantics or correctness development.

summary: Reviewed db and retire it as a general relational-database client/DSL whose theorem content is internal software invariants rather than an independent formal specification.
